description: List digital (chat) test runs in your workspace, newest first: each has an id, targetRef (the bot), kind, sector, status (pending, running, completed, failed, cancelled), outcome, how many samples were requested and judged, passed, failed and transportErrors (chats that never got a verdict), passRate, failureReason, startedAt and completedAt. Takes optional `targetRef` (exact, e.g. acme/billing-bot: only that bot's runs), `limit` (1 to 200, default 50) and `cursor` (nextCursor from the previous page; absent on the last page). Use when: the user asks how a chat bot's tests went, or for the latest digital runs. outcome and transportErrors are separate on purpose: a bot that answers well but drops chats has a delivery problem, not a behaviour one. For one run's transcript and judge reasoning use getDigitalTestRun. Voice runs are in listTestRuns, not here. Read-only. Needs digital:read.

cursor.description: Opaque base64 pagination cursor from `nextCursor` in a previous response.

limit.description: Rejected with 400 outside 1-200 rather than silently clamped.

targetRef.description: Restrict to one target (the chat analogue of a phone number).

name: listDigitalTestRuns

outputSchema.description:
One page of runs, newest first. Same cursor convention as
`GET /testing/runs`: pass `nextCursor` back as `?cursor=` for the next page.

nextCursor.description:
Opaque base64 cursor. Present ONLY when another page exists, and OMITTED
(not null) on the last page, so a generated `while (res.nextCursor)`
paginator terminates.

configId.description: Set when the run was launched from a saved DigitalTestConfig.

launchDeadline.description: Still `pending` past this means no worker ever picked the job up.

passRate.description: passed ÷ samplesJudged. Null until the run reaches a verdict.

payloadS3Bucket.description: Set when the result was too large for the response topic and was offloaded whole to S3.

items.description:
One conversation, with its own verdict and evidence. Written onto the run row
verbatim as the worker sent it, so every field the worker emits is declared here —
`packages/functions/openapi/response-contract.test.ts` fails the build if one is not.

botTurns.description: Bot turns in this conversation. Counts the bot only, so it is not the transcript length.

catalogueTestId.description: Null on the kinds that are not compliance.

items.description:
One condition the judge cited for its verdict. `condition` and `reason` are what the
judge sends today; the remaining fields are emitted by some judge versions. Treat the
object as open — an unknown key must never cost a caller their verdict.

failureReason.description: The worker emits `null` when there was no failure.

judgeModel.description: Empty string on `standard`, which reaches its verdict by matching rather than judging.

judgeRaw.description:
The judge's unparsed output, kept for audit. Deliberately untyped, which also
admits the `null` the worker sends when it kept nothing: this is whatever the
judge returned, and pinning a shape here would be a guess.

passEvidence.description: Judged kinds only. There is no combined `evidence` field.

items.description:
One condition the judge cited for its verdict. `condition` and `reason` are what the
judge sends today; the remaining fields are emitted by some judge versions. Treat the
object as open — an unknown key must never cost a caller their verdict.

sessionId.description: The transport's own conversation id. Null when the transport never connected.

startedAt.description:
No `format: date-time` on purpose — the worker emits an empty string on
samples it did not time, and declaring a format would make a truthful
payload fail validation.

items.description: Shaped like the voice `TestStepResult` so a client widens a union rather than learning a second shape.

similarity.description: Reported whatever the matcher — on a failure it distinguishes a typo from a wrong turn.

transcript.description: A list of turns, NOT a string.

items.description: One turn of the conversation, as the worker's transcript emits it.

status.description:
`failed` means the test could not be DELIVERED (an infrastructure failure,
with `failureReason` set). A bot that behaved badly produces `completed`
with `outcome: fail` — the two are deliberately not the same thing.

target.description:
What `phoneNumber` becomes on a text channel. Discriminated on `transport`.
`targetRef` (on the run, not here) is the stable human-readable identity a
report aggregates on.

oneOf.description: Amazon Connect chat via StartChatContact plus the participant websocket.

assumeRoleArn.description: Optional cross-account role. Absent means ambient credentials.

oneOf.description: Generic REST chat endpoint, including OpenAI-compatible shapes.
Browser-automated embedded chat widget, for targets with no API at all.
Amazon Lex V2 via RecognizeText. Plain request and response, no websocket.

assumeRoleArn.description: Optional cross-account role. Absent means ambient credentials.

oneOf.description:
Microsoft Bot Framework Direct Line 3.0: Copilot Studio agents and Azure Bot
Service bots. Holds a token endpoint URL, never a Direct Line secret.

directLineDomain.description:
The Direct Line host, for example `https://europe.directline.botframework.com`.
When absent it is discovered (Copilot Studio) or the global host is used.

skipStartEvent.description:
A `startConversation` event is sent when the conversation opens, which is what
makes a Copilot Studio agent greet. Set true for a bot that greets on its own.

transportErrors.description:
Samples that never produced a verdict because the transport failed. Kept
SEPARATE from `passRate`: a channel whose bot is impeccable but whose estate
drops one chat in six has a delivery problem, and folding the two together
would tell the customer to fix the wrong thing.

title: List Digital Test Runs
